questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four things a cloud AI platform bundles for you?
options: Elastic compute
A model catalog
Governance (content filters, RBAC, logging)
Guaranteed model accuracy for your specific use case
questions.explain: A cloud AI platform gives you compute, a model catalog, governance, and consolidated billing — but it never guarantees accuracy for your specific use case; that still depends on your data and evaluation.

questions.q: What hidden cost of self-hosting does the lesson call out first?
options: The need for an ongoing MLOps team to patch, scale, and monitor the stack
A one-time setup fee charged by Microsoft
Mandatory annual retraining of every model
A licensing fee paid to the cloud AI platform
questions.explain: Self-hosting requires a standing MLOps responsibility — patching, scaling, and monitoring — that doesn't show up on the GPU invoice itself.

questions.q: How is an Azure OpenAI resource created?
options: Only through a separate OpenAI.com account, unrelated to Azure
The same way as any other Azure resource — through Create a resource in the Azure portal
It is created automatically the first time you sign up for Azure
It requires a phone call to Microsoft support
questions.explain: Azure OpenAI is a standard Azure resource, created through Create a resource in the Azure portal just like a storage account or VM.

questions.q: What URL do you use to reach the Azure AI Foundry portal?
options: portal.azure.com
ai.azure.com
foundry.microsoft.com
studio.openai.com
questions.explain: Azure AI Foundry (now officially Microsoft Foundry) is reached at ai.azure.com, a separate portal from the general Azure portal.

questions.q: What does the Monitor settings panel let you configure?
options: Only the color theme of the dashboard
Your Azure subscription's billing address
Operational metrics, continuous evaluation, scheduled evaluations, red team scans, and alerts
The physical location of the datacenter
questions.explain: The Monitor settings panel is where you turn on and configure operational metrics, continuous evaluation, scheduled evaluations, red team scans, and alerts.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say AI service costs deserve extra attention compared to typical Azure resources?
options: Because price per token varies enormously by model, and usage can spike quickly from bugs or retry loops
Because Azure Cost Management doesn't support AI resources at all
Because AI services are always free
Because AI services can only be billed annually
questions.explain: A frontier model can cost many times more per token than a smaller model, and bursty usage (like a retry loop or bug) can spike spend within minutes.

questions.q: Which Python package handles authentication for Foundry SDK clients?
options: azure-identity
azure-ai-projects
requests
flask
questions.explain: azure-identity provides credential classes like DefaultAzureCredential, which handle authentication without a hardcoded key.

questions.q: What problem does retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) solve?
options: It makes models train faster
It grounds a model's answer in content it wasn't trained on, by retrieving it at request time
It eliminates the need for an API key
It automatically translates text into other languages
questions.explain: RAG retrieves relevant content from your own data and feeds it to the model as context, so answers can reflect information beyond the model's training data.

questions.q: In the index Fields screenshot, what does the 'Vector index quota usage' panel indicate?
options: That vector storage is billed and limited separately from the plain-text fields in the same index
That the index has no vector fields defined at all
The total number of documents in the storage account
The current Azure subscription's spending limit
questions.explain: That panel is a reminder that vector storage has its own quota and cost, tracked apart from the index's regular text fields.

questions.q: What does enabling a system-assigned managed identity on a VM actually require from the developer?
options: Generating and securely storing a new client secret
A single checkbox at resource creation — no secret is issued to anyone
Manually rotating a password every 90 days
Writing custom authentication code from scratch
questions.explain: A system-assigned managed identity is enabled with one checkbox, and Azure manages the underlying credential — there's no secret for a developer to handle.

questions.q: What changes in your application's SDK calls or authentication when you move from a public endpoint to a private one?
options: Nothing — the API, SDK calls, and authentication all stay identical; only the network path changes
The authentication method must switch from keys to certificates
Every SDK call must be rewritten to use a new private API
The application must be rebuilt as a container
questions.explain: A private endpoint changes the network path only — there's no public IP left to find, but the API surface and auth are unchanged.

questions.q: Why would picking an NV-series VM for model fine-tuning be a mistake, even though it has a GPU?
options: NV-series doesn't actually include a GPU
NV-series VMs can't run Linux
NV-series is tuned for visualization and virtual desktops, not training workloads
NV-series is more expensive than ND-series for the same training job
questions.explain: The GPU is there, but it's purpose-built for visualization/VDI scenarios rather than the compute pattern training workloads need.

questions.q: When you one-click deploy a model from Model Garden, what service actually ends up serving it?
options: AWS Bedrock
Azure AI Foundry
Vertex AI — the managed endpoint service underneath Model Garden
The model deploys directly to a developer's personal laptop
questions.explain: Model Garden is the catalog; Vertex AI is the managed service that actually deploys and serves the chosen model.

questions.q: Why does the lesson call out noting an embedding's dimension and distance metric explicitly?
options: Because not every provider's embedding model agrees on either one, and a silent mismatch breaks retrieval in a hard-to-debug way
Because dimension and distance metric affect billing directly
Because Azure AI Search requires a specific embedding dimension for all models
Because embeddings without a noted dimension are rejected by every cloud
questions.explain: Embedding dimension and distance metric vary by provider/model — an unnoted mismatch during a swap can silently degrade retrieval quality.

questions.q: What do Azure AI Foundry, AWS Bedrock, and Google's Vertex AI/Model Garden have in common underneath their different branding?
options: They are all exactly the same product rebranded three times
A model catalog, plus a managed service that deploys and calls whatever model is chosen from it
They all require the exact same CLI commands
They only work with each vendor's own models, with no third-party options
questions.explain: Despite different names and UIs, all three solve the same underlying problem: a catalog of models, and a managed layer to deploy and call them.

questions.q: What does the Test Agent window let you verify before an agent goes to production?
options: The agent's monthly AWS bill
Whether the agent's underlying VM has enough disk space
How a conversation unfolds turn by turn, including reviewing a tool call's output before submitting it to let the agent continue
Which AWS region has the cheapest pricing for that model
questions.explain: The Test Agent panel steps through a conversation, pausing on tool calls so you can review output before approving it to continue.

questions.q: What is the relationship between an endpoint and a deployment in this SDK workflow?
options: They are the same thing, just different names
An endpoint is the container; a deployment is the model running inside it
A deployment is created first, then wrapped in an endpoint
An endpoint can only ever hold exactly one deployment
questions.explain: A ManagedOnlineEndpoint is created first as a container, then one or more ManagedOnlineDeployment objects are deployed into it.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the most common way this capstone actually stalls?
options: Choosing a programming language the student doesn't know
The Foundry portal being unavailable
Not having an Azure account at all
Picking a model or configuration big enough that quota or cost delays it for days
questions.explain: The lesson calls out scope, not technical difficulty, as the most common reason this capstone stalls — an oversized model or deployment choice can turn into a multi-day quota or cost delay.

questions.q: What four things does this lesson recommend covering in a five-minute capstone presentation?
options: Company history, team bios, funding, and roadmap
The model, the deployment, the security, and the monitoring
Only the final invoice from Azure
A full line-by-line code review
questions.explain: The recommended walkthrough covers the model deployed, the live deployment itself, one working security control, and the monitoring setup.

questions.q: What does the az monitor diagnostic-settings create command do?
options: Deletes an endpoint's logs permanently
Deploys a new model to the endpoint
Grants public internet access to a resource
Routes a resource's logs and metrics to a destination like a Log Analytics workspace
questions.explain: A diagnostic setting is an Azure configuration that routes a resource's logs and metrics to a destination such as Log Analytics, Event Hub, or storage.
